name: José Mourinho
bio: Known for meticulous organisation, defensive solidity and ruthless counter-attacking football inspired by his greatest sides.

name: Pep Guardiola
bio: The defining positional-play coach of the modern era, favouring extreme possession, high pressing and fluid attacking rotations.

name: Carlo Ancelotti
bio: A master of adaptation who builds balanced, player-led systems and gets the best from elite attacking talent.

name: Sir Alex Ferguson
bio: Manchester United's legendary manager, famous for fearless attacking football, relentless tempo and a winning mentality inspired by his great sides.

name: Jürgen Klopp
bio: The architect of 'heavy metal football' — intense gegenpressing, rapid vertical transitions and relentless energy.

name: Arsène Wenger
bio: A pioneer of technical, flowing possession football in England, built around quick short passing and intelligent movement.

name: Antonio Conte
bio: An intensely demanding coach renowned for back-three systems, aggressive wing-backs and disciplined defensive structure.

name: Diego Simeone
bio: The face of modern defensive resilience — a fiercely compact, aggressive block that thrives on transitions and set pieces.

name: Zinedine Zidane
bio: An elegant manager who blended control with devastating transitions, guiding Real Madrid to an era of European dominance.

name: Luis Enrique
bio: A modern positional coach who emphasises possession, aggressive pressing and versatile, fluid attacking trios.

name: Marcelo Bielsa
bio: An obsessive, influential coach famous for man-oriented pressing, relentless intensity and vertical, risk-taking football.

name: Mauricio Pochettino
bio: A front-foot coach who built a dynamic, high-pressing Tottenham side around youthful energy and rapid transitions.

name: Thomas Tuchel
bio: A meticulous tactician known for back-three structures, flexible pressing and a strong emphasis on defensive control.

name: Massimiliano Allegri
bio: A pragmatic Italian coach who balances defensive solidity with efficient, opportunistic attacking football.

name: Unai Emery
bio: A detail-driven coach renowned for structured build-up, aggressive counter-pressing and set-piece organisation.

name: Simone Inzaghi
bio: A modern Italian coach whose 3-5-2 systems combine aggressive wing-backs with rapid, vertical counter-attacks.

name: Xavi Hernández
bio: A protégé of the positional-play school who emphasises central overloads, structured possession and intricate passing.

name: José Bordalás
bio: A coach synonymous with disciplined, aggressive low blocks, duels and direct football from a hard-working side.

name: Oliver Glasner
bio: An Austrian coach who favours a compact back three, aggressive transitions and rapid attacking width.

name: Andoni Iraola
bio: A Bielsa-influenced coach known for man-oriented pressing, high tempo and fearless, vertical attacking play.

name: John Herdman
bio: A British-Canadian coach who built a resilient, quick-transitioning Canada men's national team and led them to the 2022 World Cup.

name: Shin Tae-yong
bio: A South Korean coach who transformed Indonesia's national team with an aggressive, hard-working, counter-attacking identity.

name: Lionel Scaloni
bio: An adaptable coach who built a balanced, togetherness-driven Argentina side that won the 2022 World Cup.

name: Walid Regragui
bio: A coach who led Morocco to the 2022 World Cup semi-final with a brilliant, disciplined defensive block and fearless counters.

name: Sepp Herberger
bio: West Germany's 1954 World Cup-winning coach, famous for an adaptable, resilient and highly disciplined side.

name: Gusztáv Sebes
bio: Architect of the legendary 'Mighty Magyars' and the pioneering deep-lying centre-forward system of the 1950s.

name: Mário Zagallo
bio: A World Cup winner as player and coach who shaped Brazil's fluid, attacking tradition across several eras.

name: Helenio Herrera
bio: The obsessive innovator behind catenaccio, famous for defensive discipline and ruthless counter-attacking.

name: Rinus Michels
bio: The father of Total Football, whose Netherlands sides revolutionised positional interchange and pressing.

name: Carlos Alberto Parreira
bio: A pragmatic, well-travelled coach who guided Brazil to the 1994 World Cup with a balanced, organised side.

name: Guus Hiddink
bio: A master tournament coach who took South Korea to the 2002 semi-finals with fearless, high-energy football.

name: Luiz Felipe Scolari
bio: A fiery motivator who led Brazil to the 2002 World Cup with a balanced, resilient and opportunistic side.

name: Joachim Löw
bio: The coach behind Germany's 2014 World Cup triumph, built on positional play, pressing and technical quality.

name: Vicente del Bosque
bio: The calm manager who guided Spain to the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 with tiki-taka dominance.

name: Fernando Santos
bio: A pragmatic coach who led Portugal to Euro 2016 with a resilient, counter-attacking and disciplined side.

name: Didier Deschamps
bio: A serial winner who built France around defensive solidity, balance and devastating transitions.

name: Óscar Tabárez
bio: Uruguay's long-serving coach who rebuilt the national team around a fierce, organised and competitive identity.

name: Zlatko Dalić
bio: The coach who led Croatia to the 2018 World Cup final with a resilient, technically excellent midfield-driven side.

name: Hajime Moriyasu
bio: Japan's coach who built an energetic, high-pressing side that beat Germany and Spain at the 2022 World Cup.

name: Hervé Renard
bio: A tournament specialist famed for organising resilient, united teams that punch above their weight.

name: Roberto Martínez
bio: A possession-focused coach who built Belgium's golden generation around structured build-up play.

name: Luis Suárez Miramontes
bio: A Ballon d'Or-winning midfielder who later coached Spain with an emphasis on control and technique.

name: Berti Vogts
bio: The coach who led a unified Germany to Euro 1996 with an organised, battling and efficient side.

name: Carlos Bilardo
bio: The tactically obsessive coach who led Argentina to the 1986 World Cup with man-marking and pragmatism.

name: Telê Santana
bio: A romantic of Brazilian football whose 1982 side is remembered for beautiful, attack-minded play.

name: Zdeněk Zeman
bio: A fierce advocate of attacking, high-tempo football whose ideas influenced generations of coaches.

name: Otto Rehhagel
bio: The coach behind Greece's astonishing Euro 2004 triumph, built on a brilliant, disciplined low block and set-piece threat.

name: Alfred Riedl
bio: An Austrian coach and Southeast Asian specialist who had several spells in charge of Indonesia, emphasising organisation and technical play.

name: Patrick Kluivert
bio: A former Dutch striker turned coach who took charge of Indonesia for the 2026 World Cup qualifying campaign, favouring possession and attacking football.

name: Benny Dollo
bio: A respected Indonesian coach who led the national team and was a long-serving figure in Indonesian football.

name: Luis Milla
bio: A Spanish coach who brought a possession-based, positional approach to Indonesia during his time in charge.

name: Indonesia Legends XI
bio: A tribute entry representing the traditional strengths of Indonesian football — technical flair, quick wide play and passionate counter-attacking.

name: Indra Sjafri
bio: One of Indonesia's leading coaches, renowned for his work with the U-19, U-20 and U-23 national teams and for a successful spell at Bali United.
